extracted.intended_audience: patent and trademark practitioners, foreign attorneys/agents, USPTO disciplinary counsel, and stakeholders who practice before the USPTO
extracted.subtask_description: Proposed amendments to 37 CFR parts 1 and 11 setting substantive and procedural requirements governing persons who represent others before the USPTO (registration/limited recognition/reciprocal recognition, disciplinary procedures including diversion, discovery, motions, hearings, appeals, and professional independence/business-arrangement rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation in the USPTO Diversion Program (§ 11.30)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director may dispose of a disciplinary matter by entering into a diversion agreement with a practitioner before or, in extraordinary cases, after a complaint under § 11.34 is filed. Diversion agreements may provide for law office management assistance, counseling, participation in lawyer assistance programs, and attendance at continuing legal education programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility criteria (proposed § 11.30): practitioner must generally not have been disciplined by the USPTO or another jurisdiction within the past three years (except where that prior discipline was based on the same conduct forming the basis for the current investigation). The OED Director may consider mitigating and aggravating factors (citing ABA Model Rules). The program is intended for practitioners whose physical or mental health issues or law practice management issues resulted in minor misconduct. Specifics not fully addressed in § 11.30 (e.g., material breach details) will be handled in individualized diversion agreements. Neither party is obligated to propose or enter an agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct excluded from diversion (§ 11.30(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: For a practitioner to be eligible for diversion, the conduct at issue must not involve: (1) the misappropriation of funds or dishonesty, deceit, fraud, or misrepresentation; (2) substantial prejudice to a client or other person as a result of the conduct; (3) a serious crime as defined in § 11.1; or (4) a pattern of similar misconduct unless the misconduct at issue is minor and related to a chronic physical or mental health condition or disease.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This sets substantive limits on diversion eligibility; patterns of similar misconduct are generally disqualifying unless minor and health-related. Misconduct involving dishonesty, misappropriation, serious crimes, or substantial client/public prejudice precludes diversion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of diversion agreement completion and breach (§ 11.30(c)-(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: A diversion agreement is automatically completed when its terms are fulfilled. A practitioner's successful completion of the diversion agreement bars the OED Director from pursuing discipline based on the conduct set forth in the agreement. A material breach of the agreement is cause for termination of participation and may permit the OED Director to pursue discipline based on the conduct set forth in the agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Completion provides finality and protection from discipline for the specified conduct; material breaches remove that protection and restart disciplinary exposure. The OED Director retains discretion to terminate or pursue discipline on breach.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED disposal options for disciplinary investigations (§ 11.22(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: When conducting disciplinary investigations the OED Director may: (3) institute formal charges upon approval of the Committee on Discipline; (4) enter into a settlement agreement with the practitioner and submit it for USPTO Director approval; or (5) enter into a diversion agreement with the practitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diversion is an explicit disposal option alongside formal charges and settlement. The OED Director has flexibility in choosing disposition consistent with the rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal recognition — contact information and status updates (§ 11.14(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: A foreign attorney or agent granted reciprocal recognition under § 11.14(c)(1) must provide to the OED Director their postal address, at least one and up to three email addresses where they receive email, and a business telephone number, and must provide any change to such addresses and telephone number within 30 days of the date of the change. They must also notify the OED Director of any lapse in their authorization to represent clients before the trademark office in the country in which they are registered and reside.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose is to provide potential clients certainty about good standing and current contact information. Failure to update within 30 days is a ground for withdrawal of reciprocal recognition absent good cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal recognition — verification, withdrawal, and reinstatement (§ 11.14(h)-(j))
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director may send a letter to the last-provided postal address to ascertain contact information and/or good standing; recipients must provide contact information and, if requested, a certificate of good standing. Failure to reply within a specified time or to provide requested information may result in withdrawal of reciprocal recognition. Upon notice that a practitioner is no longer registered or in good standing in the relevant foreign trademark office, no longer resides in that country, or has not provided required information, the OED Director shall promptly withdraw recognition and publish notice. A withdrawn practitioner may reapply for recognition (and must pay the application fee required by § 1.21(a)(1)(i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Withdrawal does not relieve other USPTO obligations (e.g., withdrawing from pending matters). Reinstatement requires reapplication and fee payment. The rules aim to keep the public record accurate and to ensure practitioners are currently authorized where they claim recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited recognition in patent matters and immigration-based limits (§ 11.9(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual ineligible to become registered under § 11.6 because of immigration status may be granted limited recognition to practice before the Office in patent matters if the U.S. Government authorizes employment or training in the U.S. to represent a patent applicant; limited recognition is granted for a period consistent with immigration status and is subject to U.S. immigration laws and terminates if the individual ceases to lawfully reside in the U.S., maintain authorized employment or training, or maintain their immigration status. Limited recognition shall not be granted or extended to a non-U.S. citizen residing outside the United States. The term 'nonimmigrant alien' is removed as not inclusive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This clarifies eligibility and automatic termination triggers—no substantive change in practice but provides explicit regulatory wording to align with current practice and avoid overbroad terminology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elimination of fee for changing status from patent agent to patent attorney (§ 1.21 / § 11.7(l))
rubrics_metrics.description: The $110 fee in § 1.21(a)(2)(iii) charged when a registered patent agent changes their registration from agent to attorney is removed. § 11.7(l) is revised to state an agent may request registration as an attorney under § 11.6(a) and must demonstrate their good standing as an attorney.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removal is intended to incentivize agents who become attorneys to promptly update their status, improving the accuracy of the register of patent attorneys and agents. Practitioners still must demonstrate attorney good standing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowing fee sharing and business arrangements with non-practitioners subject to state rules (§ 11.504(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: The prohibitions of § 11.504(a), (b), or (d)(1) or (2) shall not apply to an arrangement that fully complies with the laws, rules, and regulations of the attorney licensing authority of a State that regulates such arrangement and in which the practitioner is an active member in good standing. This permits an attorney-practitioner to share legal fees with a non-practitioner, form a partnership with a non-practitioner, or be part of a for-profit association/corporation owned by a non-practitioner, subject to state-law compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This defers to state bars where states authorize such arrangements. However, this does not permit a non-practitioner to direct or regulate the practitioner’s professional judgment (see § 11.504(c)) nor permit practice in a form where a non-practitioner controls professional judgment (see § 11.504(d)(3)). Practitioners remain subject to all other USPTO rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motions practice — memorandum and briefing rules limited to dispositional motions (§ 11.43)
rubrics_metrics.description: Only motions for summary judgment and motions to dismiss are required to be accompanied by a written memorandum, and the prescribed time periods to file response and reply memoranda apply only to those motions. Every motion must include a statement that the moving party conferred in good faith with the opposing party and whether the motion is opposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Memoranda for dispositive motions must be double-spaced in 12-point font. Default briefing schedule: opposing party serves and files response within 21 days of service of the motion; moving party may file a reply within 14 days after service of the response, unless hearing officer extends time for good cause. Hearing officers retain discretion to require memoranda or set time limits for other motions. Parties must promptly notify the hearing officer if issues are resolved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearing procedures — videoconference and transcripts (§ 11.44)
rubrics_metrics.description: The hearing officer may order a hearing to be conducted by remote videoconference in whole or in part. Oral hearings will be recorded and transcribed, and testimony received under oath or affirmation. The hearing officer shall conduct the hearing as if subject to 5 U.S.C. 556. A copy of the transcript becomes part of the record and shall be provided to the OED Director and the respondent at the expense of the Office. For incarcerated respondents, oral hearings may be held at the location of incarceration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies current practice allowing remote hearings and that a stenographer is not required. Transcript and record rules are specified; Office bears expense of providing transcript copies to parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written discovery — motion content, authorization, and default deadlines (§ 11.52)
rubrics_metrics.description: After an answer is filed, a party may file a motion under § 11.43 seeking authorization to propound written discovery of relevant evidence, including a reasonable number of requests for admission (including genuineness of documents), interrogatories, documents for inspection and copying, and things other than documents. The motion must include the proposed discovery requests and explain in detail, for each request, how the discovery sought is reasonable and relevant to an issue actually raised in the complaint or answer; responses must include specific objections or those objections are waived.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If authorized, unless the hearing officer orders otherwise the moving party must serve authorized discovery requests within 5 days of authorization and the opposing party must serve responses within 30 days of service. The hearing officer may authorize only discovery deemed reasonable and relevant. This restructures prior paragraphs into a clearer chronological process and imposes waiver consequences for omitted objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal briefing extensions and removal of affidavit requirement (§ 11.55)
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirement to submit a supporting affidavit when moving for an extension of time to file a brief regarding an appeal of an initial decision is removed. The USPTO Director may extend the time for filing a brief upon granting a motion setting forth good cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This eliminates an unnecessarily burdensome affidavit requirement while retaining the requirement to show good cause. Also: unless the Director permits, no further briefs or motions shall be filed on appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement that motions include proof of conferral and notification if resolved (§ 11.43 first paragraph)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every motion must include a statement that the moving party or attorney has conferred with the opposing party in a good-faith effort to resolve the issues raised and whether the motion is opposed. If issues are resolved prior to decision, parties shall promptly notify the hearing officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This promotes early resolution and reduces unnecessary motion practice; lack of such certification may affect handling of motions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration transfer requirement — demonstration of attorney good standing (§ 11.7(l))
rubrics_metrics.description: An agent registered under § 11.6(b) may request registration as an attorney under § 11.6(a). The agent shall demonstrate their good standing as an attorney.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coupled with elimination of the status-change fee, practitioners must still demonstrate attorney good standing when requesting transfer from agent to attorney designation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal of reference to 'emeritus status' (§ 11.19(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The inadvertent reference to 'emeritus status' in § 11.19(a) is removed because no such status was ever finalized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial/clarifying change with no substantive effect other than removing obsolete language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application fee requirement for reciprocal recognition (§ 11.14(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual seeking reciprocal recognition under § 11.14(c)(1) must apply in writing to the OED Director and pay the application fee required by § 1.21(a)(1)(i) of the subchapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinstatement after withdrawal also requires submission of a request and payment of the application fee. This preserves the fee-based application process for initial and re-applications for reciprocal recognition.
